item.title: Using Noteweld
item.description:
Try it without an account

Open the public editor to try Markdown, preview and optional Vim. The scratchpad lives in the tab; this example does not save it to a private account. Download anything you want to keep before leaving.

Explore the public graph for an original six-note sample. It does not read private notes or start a processing job.

Create a private workspace

Open the sign-in page , or start email signup. Follow the verification email before choosing your name and passphrase. Verified email accounts can request mailed password resets. Existing recovery keys remain available; keep them out of messages and screenshots.

item.title: Using Pageweft
item.description:
See a completed result

Open Pageweft or explore the original PDF/Markdown/ZIP example linked from its website and the portfolio. Viewing the completed example does not run a GPU conversion.

Inspect before processing

Upload a PDF you have permission to process. Each file can be at most 64 MiB and 1,000 PDF pages; up to five files can be inspected, with each conversion confirmed separately. Choose the original PDF page numbers or ranges and review the text-layer inspection and quote.

item.title: Using Sonaweft
item.description:
Hear a completed example

Open the completed scientific example to hear a human-voiced NOAA interview about gravity, follow actual recognition text and download a hashed bundle. Prepared listening notes are labeled separately from optional review-provider output. This precomputed example does not start another transcription job.

Upload and inspect

The hosted workflow accepts authorized English audio/video up to 64 MiB and 60 minutes. Upload a file and inspect its duration/quote before confirming work. The hosted application does not download arbitrary platform URLs or use your browser cookies.

item.title: Using the vanilla demo
item.description:
Open the portfolio demo

Open the bundled demo or launch it from the portfolio’s vanilla JavaScript card. This is a separate implementation from Noteweld. It demonstrates native browser APIs rather than the professional Next.js application.

Work in one browser

Try notes and checklists, pin/color/label controls, archive and trash. Storage belongs to this browser and website origin. It does not create a cloud account, synchronize devices or inherit Noteweld’s editor/graph features.

item.title: How the environment fits together
item.description:
Start with the source

NixOS configuration repository · Published Neovim configuration

The public NixOS repository is the published baseline. The local security maintenance verified on 16 October has not yet been committed to that repository. The interactive guide uses short, explanatory examples; it is not a copy of private machine state.

Two configuration layers

The flake pins Nixpkgs, Home Manager and Fenix. NixOS declares system packages, hardware integration and services. Home Manager declares user packages and configuration links. The system build integrates both layers, so package/configuration changes can be reviewed together.

item.title: Why these previews run on Modal
item.description:
More than a GPU rental

Modal runs application containers on CPU as well as GPU resources. It supports HTTP applications, background functions, schedules, persistent volumes and secrets. An HTTP server can be Python/FastAPI or a Node process; the deployment wrapper does not require every application to be written in Python.

Official references: HTTP applications , autoscaling , persistent volumes and secrets . Checked on 16 October 2026; provider policies and prices can change.

The current deployment

Component Hosting Persistent state
Portfolio, vanilla demo and this Hugo library GitHub Pages Static versioned files; vanilla demo uses browser storage
Pageweft web/API and extraction jobs Modal CPU containers and A10G workers Separate document and serialized SQLite ledger volumes
Sonaweft web/API, speech and review coordination Modal CPU containers and L4 workers Separate media, model-cache and serialized SQLite ledger volumes
Noteweld web/API Modal Node/Next.js CPU container Isolated Neon PostgreSQL; encrypted backups in Modal

Paddle handles commercial payments rather than hosting these websites. DeepSeek is an optional text-inference provider for Sonaweft. No shared customer wallet or login is implemented. Linguavell is a separate startup project.

item.title: Neovim: find, edit, inspect
item.description:
Follow a small loop

Find a file, make a focused change, inspect diagnostics, format it, and run the relevant check. The editor shortens that loop; it does not establish that a change is correct.

The configured leader is Space. These mappings come from the published Neovim source , inspected alongside the local checkout.

Action Configured mapping Tool
Find project files Space, s, f Telescope
Search file contents Space, s, g Telescope live grep
Remember a working file Space, a Harpoon
Open the remembered-file menu Ctrl + e Harpoon
Format a buffer Space, f Conform
Move between editor splits Ctrl + h / j / k / l Neovim window navigation

Language support through Nix

The Neovim wrapper supplies language-server and formatter executables: gopls, TypeScript language server, nil, Pyright, clangd, Lua language server, Marksman and rust-analyzer among them. Formatting tools include Stylua, nixfmt, gofumpt, Black and Ruff.

item.title: Building Noteweld: accounts to connected notes
item.description:
Start from the evidence

The current source is connected-notes handoff f6901ff (owner-access source record). Application code for that collection is e1b8740; earlier foundations are not descriptions of every current feature. Read the usage guide before following the implementation record.

1. Repair account and note persistence

The early registration work validated identity/password input, seeded accounts and preserved failed form input. The then-selected Neon HTTP adapter supported a batch operation rather than interactive transaction callbacks. Its mocked-transport checks were explicitly not evidence of database rollback.

item.title: Building Pageweft: extraction to a hosted workbench
item.description:
1. Establish actual extraction

The initial requirement was private PDF-to-Markdown preparation using MinerU on the owner’s Modal account. The design moved from customer-provided Modal credentials to owner-hosted processing; customers do not provide cloud tokens. MinerU 2.7.6 runs in a cloud GPU image and retains original engine output. The laptop’s 2 GB GPU is not required.

A bounded one-page public trial was verified before describing full-book processing. The initial deployed web startup failed because modal_fn.py was missing from its uploaded source. Explicit inclusion fixed the image, followed by a fresh deployment and public workflow checks. Original verification record .

item.title: Building Sonaweft: speech, source and recovery
item.description:
Source chronology

The original instascript command and import paths remain compatible. Hosted workbench 7fde01a (owner-access source record) added the upload/review/export workflow. 5ac1d7c added the original completed audio example; handoff 68b8472 (owner-access source record) normalized artifacts and corrected the provider reference. The old optional Claude/vault documents are archives, not required setup.

1. Preserve source and recover work

The standalone CPU CLI uses FFmpeg/FFprobe and faster-whisper. Immutable original recognition, separate corrections, generated notes and sourced questions became distinct artifacts. Private checkpoints, exclusive locks, completion hashes and atomic publication support deliberate recovery; cross-path perceptual deduplication is not promised.

item.title: Building the vanilla Keep demo
item.description:
Keep the two implementations separate

This is the vanilla JavaScript/localStorage application, not Noteweld. Native DOM modules, Webpack, checklists, labels, colors, pin/archive/trash and browser storage form its implementation. Existing source history includes f6bc24ce for labels/search/filter/demo notes and 64471b8d for an unused import cleanup.

The 16 October reliability release incorporates the preserved local changes and intentional tracked-dependency cleanup. Source commit a03b0ed1 publishes the browser reliability work; the portfolio refresh copies its production bundle. Earlier statements below describe the baseline they reviewed.

item.title: How to review these projects
item.description:
Start with behavior

Open a project’s usage guide and its live or completed example. Identify the intended action, what should persist, the expected failure behavior and the current limits. A polished cover illustration is not a running backend.

Follow the implementation

Read the technical overview, then the specific architecture/editor/connections manual. Imported documents link an exact committed source revision. A local documentation edition is marked when it includes uncommitted documentation changes; the link then identifies the committed baseline.

item.title: Maintaining this documentation library
item.description:
Source and publication

The actual portfolio repository contains documentation/ for Hugo source and manuals/ for generated static output. The existing GitHub Pages root serves both the portfolio and /manuals/. No application server, visitor login, external font, analytics service or search API is needed.

Hugo 0.156.0 is the recorded build version. Imported project README/docs files are explicitly listed in documentation/manifest.json; this is not a recursive copy of the workspace. Current usage guides and journal entries are authored directly in Hugo content.

item.title: Build, activate, verify, recover
item.description:
Review before changing the system

Inspect Git state and the relevant diff. Back up files being changed privately. Preserve unrelated work, the current lock file and a known working boot generation. New files referenced by a Git-backed flake must be deliberately included in its source.

Use a Git-filtered flake source. An explicit unfiltered path: source may include ignored private files before a build-time check can reject them.

Match the check to the change

Change Relevant evidence
Documentation Generated pages, links, keyboard and browser checks
User-profile application Package build, executable, launch and a real file operation
NixOS service Option evaluation, system build, activation and actual service behavior
Graphics/kernel update Supported hardware branch, complete build, rollback route and controlled boot acceptance
Backup procedure Retained-data fixtures, successful real copy and a separate restore test

For this machine, the nr shortcut runs sudo nixos-rebuild switch against the NixOS flake. It does not decrypt secrets, stage files or commit changes. Administrative authentication remains an operating-system boundary.

item.title: From extracted files to retained sources
item.description:
A complete portable path

Pageweft extracts selected PDF pages, lets the reader review original text and explicit corrections, and exports a hashed archive. Sonaweft retains original recognition, user corrections and optional advisory notes as separate outputs. Noteweld previews and validates those archives, imports notes and source files atomically, and keeps private original bytes available separately from later edits.

The original public Pageweft example was regenerated with the current CPU exporter. Its v1 schema, note index, hashes and relative references validate in Noteweld. The portfolio copy matches that original fixture; it contains no private book/customer content.

item.title: Making transcript review recoverable
item.description:
The user problem

A transcript can be corrected successfully while the editing workflow still loses valuable work. In-tab undo is insufficient after a reload, and a revision number prevents conflicting saves without keeping the earlier text. Sonaweft now keeps bounded, durable annotation snapshots and lets the owner compare and restore them. The original recognition remains a separate source throughout.

Try the live workbench or read the history usage guide . A completed original example is readable without consuming processing credit.

item.title: Technical overview
item.description:

Drive uploads go directly to Google, retain retry state while the editor is open, and never fall back to managed storage. The destination is remembered per account in this browser. Usage/setup and evidence (source repository requires access), storage/privacy boundaries .

Existing private R2 media, verified-email signup/reset, account storage management, appearance controls and 15-minute Drive consent/expiry recovery are preserved. Production stays Free; checkout remains disabled pending Paddle approval and actual sandbox acceptance. Own-server storage, end-to-end encryption, native Neovim and offline desktop are not implemented.

item.title: Source and implementation notes
item.description:
A free, browser-only notes and checklist demo built with native DOM APIs, CSS, localStorage and Webpack. It shares Noteweld’s product family and deliberately has no account, server or paid features. The existing Keep repository and public URL are preserved.

Live demo · Source · Portfolio and manuals

Features

  • Create and edit notes and checklists; pin, color, label, archive, trash and restore them.
  • Search titles, bodies, labels and checklist text from either search control.
  • Use keyboard navigation, named controls and a focus-contained edit dialog; Escape saves and returns focus.
  • Export versioned JSON including archived/trashed notes and labels; validate and merge imports without replacing existing IDs.
  • Preserve drafts when a storage write fails, display an error and allow retry.
  • Recover raw stored JSON if existing notes are malformed, without silently resetting user data.
  • Use a responsive layout with readable colored notes and reduced-motion support.

Delete from Archive moves to recoverable Trash. Delete forever and Empty Trash require confirmation. There is no automatic seven-day purge. Header Refresh reloads this browser view; the layout control switches compact display. Placeholder reminders/settings are omitted from the available controls.

item.title: Markdown and Vim editing
item.description:
Open a text note or choose Take a note…. Checklists keep their separate checklist editor.

  • Write, Preview and Split change the view without discarding source or enhanced-editor undo. Split stacks vertically on narrow screens.
  • Standard keys work by default. Vim enables normal/insert/visual modes, motions, selection and Vim undo. Use i to insert, Escape to return to normal, v to select and u to undo. Escape in Vim stays inside the note.
  • Simple text provides a native textarea for accessibility, device compatibility or enhanced-editor loading failure. Switching to/from it starts fresh enhanced-editor undo; source is retained. Settings apply to this editing session.
  • Undo, Redo, Find and the formatting buttons work in the enhanced editor. Find includes replacement. Tab leaves the editor instead of trapping keyboard focus.
  • Save or Ctrl/Cmd-S writes through the normal API. Vim :w uses the same path. Existing notes stay open after these saves; Save & close also closes. Saving a new note completes its creation. Escape/backdrop closure asks before discarding an edited note; it does not silently save it.
  • A failed save leaves the draft and undo available. If another tab changed the note, copy or download the draft before Reload saved version. Reloading is a deliberate replacement and clears the old draft’s undo history. There is no durable server revision archive yet.
  • Download .md exports the exact current body, including unsaved changes, with the title as a portable filename. It does not insert a heading or modify stored data. Account JSON export still includes all notes and labels.

Media attachments — 6 November

In a signed-in note, use Attach media or drop/paste a file. Preview displays owned images, audio and video; Manage attachments reuses or removes account files. Checklists expose the same body under Attachments and details. Free accounts have 100 MB storage, 10 MB images and 25 MB audio/video files. Removing one file makes its references unavailable wherever used. Markdown/JSON exports contain references/metadata; download original media separately. See the media manual and hosted evidence (source repository requires access).

item.title: Conversion product design
item.description:
Implementation update

The approved core features are now implemented: full-book/range inspection (bounded at 64 MiB/1,000 pages), batch inspection, quotes, bounded section processing, selective retries/force OCR, source-linked review, corrections/history, portable outputs and prepaid-credit accounting. Read BOOK-RELEASE.md for tested evidence and limits. Earlier candidate language below describes the design rationale. Actual merchant activation and comparative difficult-document fidelity remain unverified; these features do not certify every source symbol.

Pageweft: conversion utility

User clarification, 14 October 2026: PDF-to-Markdown for serious work with books, including Linguavell preparation. Users control the downstream reading/LLM workflow. No study platform, AI chat, automatically generated teaching materials or decorative feature expansion.

item.description:

Preserve instascript imports/command and existing remote URLs. Noteweld is now the professional notes product; its importer is not implemented merely because Sonaweft exports bundles.

item.title: Links, backlinks and graphs
item.description:
Choose Link note while writing to insert a stable reference such as [[note:UUID|Readable caption]]. Search titles/labels, select a note and insert; the editor keeps your cursor position and undo. Escape closes the picker and returns focus. A stable ID survives a rename; its optional caption remains the text you wrote, while the link tooltip shows the current title. Copy a stable reference from any note’s detail page too.

You can also type [[Title]] or [[Title|caption]]. Matching uses trimmed, case-folded NFKC titles across your own active and archived notes. Exactly one match resolves. Duplicate titles show ambiguous; missing titles show unavailable. These are name lookups, not permanent identity: use the picker for links that must survive renames or replacement by another note with the same title. Empty titles cannot be looked up by name; link them by ID. No note is created or rewritten automatically.

item.title: Processing architecture
item.description:
Browser --> secure cookie + CSRF --> FastAPI / Modal
 |--> serialized SQLite ledger writer
 |--> private media volume (48-hour TTL)
 |--> confirmed CPU coordinator
 |--> FFmpeg normalization
 |--> L4 / faster-whisper large-v3
 |--> optional DeepSeek text review
 |--> committed result --> settle hold
Review player / separate corrections / portable exports <--|
Explicit selected claim --> Crossref metadata candidates

Isolated checkout --> Paddle --> signed durable inbox
 |--> fresh transaction + all adjustment pages
 |--> intent/owner/product-bound credit or revocation

instascript/contract.py validates original ASR and exact source-quoted review and creates versioned exports. pipeline.py provides local private checkpoints, exclusive locks, completion hashes and atomic publication. review.py bounds text/output, validates JSON and has no autonomous tools. Local source.py downloads are never invoked for public uploads.

item.title: Source bundles and provenance
item.description:
Import, review, edit

  1. Export a fresh supported ZIP from Pageweft (plain, Obsidian or LLM preset) or Sonaweft. The original PDF/recording is included only if that exporter actually includes it. Keep your own original outside the service.
  2. Sign in to Noteweld and choose Source bundles. Select the ZIP and Validate and preview. This parses and verifies it without saving notes.
  3. Review filenames, categories, excerpts, file counts and archive SHA256. Original extraction, user corrections and AI notes retain distinct labels. Hashes validate internal consistency, not provenance authenticity, model accuracy or legal rights.
  4. Choose Use existing notes (default) or deliberately create another note copy. Confirm that you may retain the files, then Import all notes together. All notes and their immutable archive commit in one transaction. A failed import saves neither. Retrying a lost acknowledgement with the same operation ID does not duplicate notes.
  5. Open an imported note, edit and save normally. Private relative assets/source links resolve through owner-checked URLs; links between imported notes use stable internal IDs. Raw ZIP bytes remain unchanged. Your edited note is separate from its original source.
  6. Download the original ZIP any time within the preview’s artifact traffic allowance. Deleting a retained source preserves its notes but makes their source/asset links unavailable. Deleting your account removes both from live storage. Operator backups expire after seven days.

Format and safety boundaries

Supported: pageweft-export/v1 in MANIFEST.json with explicit files and notes; instascript-export/v1 in manifest.json for Sonaweft. Old Pageweft demonstration archives without the current schema/index need a fresh export. Arbitrary ZIPs, vaults and account/wallet migrations are not accepted.

item.title: Connected notes release
item.description:
Original record: Connected notes release — 16 October 2026.

Milestone 005 adds stable ID wiki-link insertion, safe code-aware resolution, explicit missing/ambiguous titles, owned metadata, linked-note detail pages, outgoing/backlink panels, a bounded/filterable graph and an account-free original graph example. See the guide for exact syntax, limits and architecture.

Local evidence

Forty unit/React checks and 14 actual PostgreSQL checks passed, including parser escapes/code/GFM URL boundaries, rename/ambiguity/foreign-ID semantics, maximum graph bounds/layout and actual archive/trash/foreign metadata isolation. item.title: Book conversion release
item.description:
Original record: Book conversion release — 14 October 2026.

Implemented in the hosted Pageweft application; supersedes the one-page-only product and $1/month access proposal. Amir delegated a better pricing model and approved the conversion utility improvements. The public free sample remains one selected page, but inspection accepts books and paid jobs use separately funded credits.

Features and implementation

Capability Implementation
Books / ranges / batch inspection Up to five PDFs, each <=64 MiB and 1,000 source PDF pages; strict PDF validation and page-range parser; retained inspected PDFs can be resumed. Each conversion is separately confirmed.
Preview and price before extraction Source page count, selected pages and text-layer samples are inspected without GPU work; fixed tariff quote must match the confirmation.
Automatic / force OCR / cheaper text-only Pinned unmodified MinerU 2.7.6 uses its documented mode/language options; pypdf text-only worker uses no GPU and explicitly excludes OCR, image extraction and layout reconstruction.
Bounded sections / partial recovery Selected pages split into groups of 20; at most two GPU workers. Successful sections survive failures; explicit retries select missing or chosen original pages and can force OCR. Duplicate requests cannot reserve or dispatch twice.
Traceability / fidelity review Original page indices are mapped from the subset PDF back to the full source. Renderer preserves recognized headings, equations, HTML tables, captions, footnotes and images. Unhandled blocks, unmapped content, empty/short output, missing images and replacement glyphs are reported. Untouched engine output is retained separately; flags do not certify correctness.
Corrections / history Plain Markdown editor with original-PDF page link, optimistic edit versions and saved history. Reprocessing retains user corrections. Engine text can be loaded explicitly into the editor draft.
Portable outputs Single Markdown, individual pages, bounded page groups, or sections based on original PDF bookmarks. Local image paths, source hash, unavailable-page list, raw section extraction and review metadata. Source PDF inclusion is optional.
Cancel / discard / delete / expiry Queued work releases reserved allowance. A running cancelled section may finish and be charged. Job deletion removes edits/output and releases an unshared source. Unused inspected sources can be discarded. Hourly cleanup removes 48-hour-expired files; balances/recovery persist separately.
Account / purchase recovery Encrypted Secure/HttpOnly session; high-entropy recovery key stored only as keyed hash. One-time purchase keys can restore the owning account. No customer Modal credentials.
Payments / refunds Separate one-time pack integration verifies scoped provider orders and signed events; duplicate orders grant once, full/partial refunds revoke pack credits. Atomic reserve/settle/release accounting in integer 1/10,000 USD units. Public test-mode grants disabled. Live seller configuration remains absent.

The active HTTP factory is web/studio.py. web/main.py and web/billing.py preserve the retired interface/verifier for regression/compatibility work; they are not the public paid implementation. Books use /ledger/books.sqlite, separate from the original /ledger/state.sqlite. Each is owned by one serialized function. Do not run a second Modal app with a separate book_store function on the same volume. Owner verification scripts invoke deployed functions instead.

If it has expired, choosing an action explains the requirement and focuses the confirmation field; it does not change an identity. item.title: Quality and cost measurement
item.description:
Offline scoring

scripts/score_quality.py compares human-prepared comparable text and observed measurements. It never uploads files, calls a model, spends credits or silently changes app limits. It reports exact character/word edit rates, not factual correctness or a calibrated confidence badge. Case, punctuation, numeric values, diacritics and technical symbols remain significant; only Unicode NFC and CRLF representation normalize. Whitespace splits word tokens, so CER is generally the more useful measure for languages without space-delimited words.

item.title: Recoverable transcript review
item.description:
Sonaweft keeps the original machine transcript unchanged. Corrections and speaker labels are your annotations. Their latest 20 saved states now survive a reload or recovered workspace, for as long as the recording itself remains available.

Use saved history

  1. Open a completed result with Review & export.
  2. Expand Saved edit history and choose Load saved history.
  3. Choose a version. Changed passages show the current saved text/label beside the selected version. Reading history never replaces the editor draft.
  4. Save any unfinished correction or speaker label first. Select Restore this version as a new save and confirm the scope: every annotation in this result, rather than only the passage currently selected.
  5. Restoration creates a new revision. Retained earlier saves and the original ASR remain available; another tab cannot silently overwrite a newer revision.

The comparison is plain inert text, including source material that resembles HTML. The current save is marked explicitly. A result changed in another tab must be reopened before restoring; failed requests preserve the saved result and draft. Inputs are temporarily disabled during an annotation write to prevent lost typing. Refreshing listening/glossary cues preserves both drafts instead of resetting the editor, and a response for an earlier result cannot change the newly opened one.
